title: Geometric Dynamics of Outer Galactic Disks and Baryonic Scaling
content: We investigate galactic rotation curves and baryonic scaling within a covariant teleparallel extension of gravity. Starting from a quadratic torsion-vector contribution to the gravitational action, we derive the field equations for stationary, axisymmetric configurations and examine circular geodesic motion in the weak-field regime. We show that the resulting solutions contain distinct baryonic and homogeneous contributions, allowing Newtonian behavior in the inner regions and approximately flat rotation curves in the finite outer-disk regime, while additional modes may describe the intermediate transition. By extending the analysis to the nonstationary sector, we show that the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation \(V_f^4=G_N M_b a_0\), with \(a_0\propto cH\), can emerge under appropriate global matching and boundary conditions. The absolute normalization remains dependent on the global boundary-value solution. We examine the phenomenological predictions using 175 SPARC galaxies and 3391 resolved measurements. The leading zero-mode approximation improves the outer-disk predictions relative to baryons alone, while discrepancies in the inner regions motivate the inclusion of the remaining transition modes.
